idiom_name: frozen dataclass event + handler registry keyed by event class (or broker client)
implementation_notes: A frozen dataclass is the event: @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) raises FrozenInstanceError on assignment and gives value equality/hashing, which is all the immutability the contract needs - no base class or subclass per event type is required, because Python dispatches on the class object anyway. The channel is a small registry (a defaultdict(list) mapping the event class to handler callables) or, in an async service, an asyncio.Queue consumed by a worker task; cross-process delivery goes through a client (aiokafka, pika, celery) with the payload JSON-encoded and the type carried in a field or header. The classic 'Event base class + listener list' form survives where a framework dictates it (Django signals, PyQt signals); new code rarely needs it.
pitfalls: frozen=True is shallow: a list or dict field is still mutable, so the published fact can change under later handlers.
frozen plus eq=True makes the dataclass hashable only if every field is hashable - a list field raises TypeError in the registry; use tuples or field(compare=False).
A handler exception aborts the dispatch loop and starves later subscribers; isolate per-handler failures (log and continue) or run handlers in separate tasks.
Holding process-local handler references keeps objects alive (listener leak) and breaks pickling of events sent to multiprocessing/Celery.
